messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike of CUDA OOMs on decode/stream nodes in us-west-2. 5xx rate up to 14% on /v1/stream. Paging oncall.

maria: paging in — oncall here. seeing repeated 'CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY' from decode pods.

raj: reading logs now. looks correlated with a sudden uptick of long-running streaming requests (clients sending very large max_tokens).

sasha: confirming: ingress telemetry shows many requests with header max_tokens=20000 around 15:22 UTC. some SDKs defaulted to unlimited.

maria: customer impact? which tenants?

support-bot: affected customers: alpha-fin, notesly, 3 internal test keys. errors are producing 502/503 on streaming endpoints.

olivia: alpha-fin reported partial transcripts dropped. Severity P1 given customer-facing failures.

raj: immediate mitigation plan: 1) apply global route-level emergency cap on max_tokens=1024 for streaming endpoints, 2) enable decode throttling policy on us-west-2 pool, 3) roll fallback to smaller quantized model for bad requests.

maria: on it — adding an emergency routing override via Console API.

maria: API call: 
```
curl -X POST https://console.api.redwood/overrides \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' \
  -d '{"scope":"us-west-2","route":"/v1/stream","override":{"max_tokens":1024,"enforce":true}}'
```

maria: override applied. verifying on telemetry...

sasha: within 30s we've seen a drop in new OOMs, but a tail of processes still crashing (eviction/pager kicking in). need to drain existing pods gracefully.

raj: draining decode-pod replicas with label decode=streaming in us-west-2: `kubectl cordon && kubectl drain --grace-period=30 --timeout=3m` — doing rollout to replace with higher-swap nodes.

olivia: note: one of the failures shows kv-cache growth anomaly — a loop of repeated prefix appends caused KV size to explode per session leading to memory pressure. might be client-side prompt bug + missing token guard.

maria: copying that: recommend adding per-session KV size cap in runtime as follow-up. quickfix is route-level max_tokens cap + reject oversized prefix requests.

eric: logs snippet from pod decode-7f9b: 
```
2026-03-15T15:22:34Z ERROR decode: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (requested 1536MB)
2026-03-15T15:22:34Z ERROR decode: backtrace: runtime::gpu::allocate_cache+0x1a3
2026-03-15T15:22:34Z ERROR decode: request_id=abc123 session_id=zz9, max_tokens=20000
```

sasha: also seeing container restart loops on two nodes — node flaps from eviction due to swap pressure. filed node-alert in infra.

incident-bot: ONCALL HANDOFF: maria -> raj in 30m. Use channel for status updates.

maria: handoff ack. moving to triage doc and will publish postmortem stub.

raj: operational note: we temporarily enabled an autoscale burst (dedicated-reserve) to add 4 decode workers to take load while draining the flapping ones. needs sign-off from infra.

olivia: customer comms: support should send alpha-fin a ticket: explain root cause is runaway generation due to misconfigured max_tokens in requests; we applied emergency cap and are recovering. Provide ETA 1 hour for full recovery and offer logs.

support-bot: creating incident ticket INC-2026-324 for alpha-fin, notesly. assigning to support: @support-team.

eric: quick playbook for next steps (short):
- enforce route override (done)
- drain & replace flapping pods (in progress)
- scale up decode pool temporarily (done)
- blacklist offending client keys if abuse (pending)
- instrument and alert on KV growth per-session (follow-up)

sasha: also pushing a hotfix to runtime to treat any request with max_tokens>5000 as suspicious and return 429 instead of letting decode attempt allocation. patch ready: `runtime/guards/max_tokens_suspect` — will canary 1 pod.

maria: canary applied to 1 pod in us-west-2. monitoring.

raj: metrics: 5xxs down from 14% -> 3.2% within 5 minutes of override + drain. request drop rate still about 0.4% for existing sessions.

olivia: support update draft: "We've applied an emergency limit to streaming token lengths to protect service availability. You may see truncated responses if your app requested extremely large token counts. We're investigating a permanent guard."

maria: post-incident actions (A/FR):
- permanent server-side max_tokens ceiling and KV size cap
- SDK defaults to safe max (e.g., 1024) and warn when client overrides above envelope
- better telemetry on per-session KV growth and token budget alarms
- add runtime OOM graceful degrade to return structured error with partial payloads instead of hard 5xx
- customer outreach scheduled by support

raj: handing off active incident to infra for node stabilization. oncall shift ends in 30m — leaving notes.

maria: thanks team. I'll open full postmortem draft and include logs + timeline. closing incident thread after infra confirms node stability and 5xxs under SLO. :white_check_mark:

support-bot: INCIDENT NOTES: root cause = runaway generation (client-supplied large max_tokens) + missing server-side guard -> kernel-level CUDA OOM -> pod evictions -> request drops. mitigations: emergency routing override, pod drains, autoscale burst, runtime suspect-guard canary. follow-ups assigned.

sasha: adding timeline entry: 15:21 alert triggered -> 15:22 override applied -> 15:26 throttle & drain started -> 15:30 autoscale burst -> 15:35 5xxs down to 3% -> 15:48 steady under SLO.

maria: closing thread for now. will update when postmortem is published.
